newsitem.title: USA: FDIC's Helfer rejects curtailing deposit insurance.
newsitem.headline: FDIC's Helfer rejects curtailing deposit insurance.

text.p: Proposals to privatize or scale back federal bank deposit insurance would put the entire U.S. banking system in jeopardy, the chairman of the insurance fund said on Friday.

"Proposals to change our system by lessening coverage or privatizing deposit insurance would undermine public confidence in the banking system," chairman Ricki Helfer told a meeting of the Independent Bankers Association of America here. "A recent proposal to change the way we resolve the largest bank failures would destroy the federal deposit insurance system, if enacted."
"For federal deposit insurance to work, the coverage must be comprehensive and universal," she added.

No legislation is pending in congress to curtail or privatize deposit insurance, but some industry participants have suggested recently that such reform is needed. They said the current system encouraged banks to take excessive risks while leaving taxpayers saddled with the costs.
Helfer, who said recently that she would step down by June 1 after serving as chairman for two and one-half years, argued that a private insurance fund could not handle a rash of bank failures.

"Private insurance plans may be able to handle isolated failures successfully, but our experience in this century and the last one is that limited plans have difficulty handling failures in waves and, therefore, are not good at stemming panic or contagion and cannot assure stability," Helfer said.
